title: StaRTrEc in vascular surgery - Statin-mediated Regulatory T-cell Expansion for protection from cardio-vascular events in vascular surgery patients
summary:
The main purpose of the study is to examine whether guideline-based statin therapy in vascular surgery can influence the number of certain circulatory defense cells (regulatory T cells, TRegs).

There are currently references in the literature that higher values ​​of the above Could protect immune cells from adverse cardiovascular events.

Patients who are prescribed statin therapy in accordance with the guidelines for an indication for vascular surgery should be checked for the number of o.g. Defense cells are examined. On the day of the operation, the number of immune cells should be determined again and the corresponding difference calculated.

Potential study participants are patients who are at least 18 years old and who have not yet taken any stages at the time of the indication for vascular surgery.

The aim is to check whether a newly started stain therapy has an impact on the number of immune cells circulating in the blood. The null hypothesis is:
Statin therapy started de novo preoperatively does not induce expansion of regulatory T cells in the peripheral blood of vascular surgery patients. The corresponding Alternative hypothesis is:
Statin therapy started de novo preoperatively induces an expansion of regulatory T cells in the peripheral blood of vascular surgery patients.

interventions.name: On the day of the indication for a vascular surgical operation, study patients are ordered statins in accordance with the guidelines and blood is taken to quantify the Tregs, provided there is no therapy with statins. The Tregs are quantified again on the day of the operation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Consent, 18 years or older, planned start of preoperative statin therapy, elective, inpatient vascular surgery within the next 28 days
Exclusion criteria:
Statin therapy within the past 28 days, pregnancy, breastfeeding, contraindication to statin therapy, condition after splenectomy, myocardial infarction, stroke or acute heart failure diagnosed in the past 28 days
